name: Centro Historico
tagline: The old streets behind the Avenida, with the fish market
description: Setubal's historic core between the Avenida Luisa Todi and the Church of Jesus, a grid of narrow pedestrian streets holding the market, the sardine restaurants and most of the town's daily life. It is compact, flat and unpolished in a way the Lisbon tourist quarters no longer are.
bestFor: Anyone here for the grilled fish, the market and a short walk to everything
pros: The fish market and the sardine restaurants at the door
Pedestrian streets and everything within ten minutes
Ferry to Troia and the train to Lisbon both close
cons: Traffic and noise on the Avenida

name: Bela Vista and the Northern Districts
tagline: Residential blocks uphill, the cheapest rents in town
description: The residential districts climbing north away from the estuary, built as apartment blocks with supermarkets, schools and the town's main hospital. Nothing here is picturesque, but the flats are larger and considerably cheaper than in the centre and the bus links down to the station are frequent.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting space at the lowest rent, with a bus into the centre
pros: Larger flats and everyday shopping nearby
Frequent buses to the centre and station
cons: Uphill walk back from the centre
No restaurants or nightlife of its own

name: Praia da Saude and the Estuary Front
tagline: West along the water towards Arrabida
description: The strip running west from the centre along the Sado estuary, with small beaches, a promenade and apartment buildings facing the water and the Troia sand spit opposite. It is where the town's dolphins are most often spotted, and the road continues into the Arrabida park a few minutes further on.
bestFor: Stays that want the estuary view and Arrabida five minutes away
pros: Arrabida park and its coves a short drive west
Dolphins regularly visible from the shore
cons: Rents above the centre for a sea view
Fifteen to twenty minutes on foot into town

name: Setubal Estacao and Monte Belo
tagline: Around the station, best for the Lisbon commute
description: The area around the railway station and the streets behind it, which matters here more than usual: the train to Lisbon runs from this point and it is what makes Setubal viable as a cheaper base for the capital. Mixed housing, everyday shops and a five-minute walk to the historic centre.
bestFor: People using Setubal as a cheaper base with regular trips into Lisbon
pros: Trains to Lisbon from the doorstep
Five minutes on foot to the old centre
cons: Station-area streets are functional rather than pleasant

name: Azeitao
tagline: Wine villages on the far side of the Arrabida ridge
description: A pair of villages about twelve kilometres northwest, on the inland side of the Arrabida hills, known for Moscatel de Setubal, the Jose Maria da Fonseca winery and the local sheep's cheese. Quiet, rural and green, with the coast reachable over the ridge and Lisbon a short motorway run.
bestFor: Stays that want countryside, wine and a car, not a town
pros: Wineries and the cheese producers on the doorstep
Quick motorway access to both Lisbon and the coast
cons: Very limited services and nothing at night
